log.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Gengar

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blaziken. Lead Whimsicott+Gengar: Gengar outspeeds Floette (178>144), resists Fairy, and fires 2x Sludge Bomb (59-100% OHKO range); Whimsicott sets Tailwind so my mid-speeds lap Scarf Dragapult, or Prankster Stun Spore paralyzes a Dragapult lead before it moves. Back two: Mega Blaziken (212 Atk/167 Spe, 334 in Tailwind) cleans with CC for Arcanine-H and Knock Off for the Ghost trio; Gyarados gives Intimidate vs their five physical attackers, 4x Waterfall into Arcanine-H, Ice Fang
decisions.notebook: Verified corrections to my build notes: Close Combat is only 2x (not 4x) into Arcanine-H; Annihilape is IMMUNE to Close Combat (use Knock Off/Flare Blitz/Moonblast instead); Light of Ruin is neutral into Whimsicott; U-turn only neutral into Whimsicott; Gengar resists Fairy 0.5x. Damage ranges: Gengar Sludge Bomb vs Floette 59-100% (possible OHKO); Gengar Shadow Ball vs Dragapult 67-126%. Speed facts: Scarf Dragapult ~267-319 outspeeds my whole team until Tailwind or Prankster Stun Spore (75% acc, +1 priority beats it; Dragapult not powder-immune); paralyzed Scarf Dragapult ~133-160 < Gengar 178. Mega Blaziken exact: 157/212/100/135/100/167; 250 after one boost, 334 in Tailwind. Arcanine-H carries Lum Berry (cures one Will-O-Wisp); Annihilape has Defiant (Intimidate gives +2 Atk — avoid Gyarados switch into it). Plan: Whimsicott+Gengar lead, Tailwind mode, Mega Blaziken+Gyarados back; Kingambit/Excadrill benched this game (Kingambit 4x weak to Annihilape, loses to Arcanine; Excadrill EQ clashes with Blaziken).

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Floette. Lead Floette+Arcanine: T1 Intimidate physicals, Mega Fairy Aura pressure Whims/Gengar/Gyarados, Rock Slide/ES chip. Back Annihilape+Basculegion complete the mode—4x CC Kingambit, Adapt Wave Crash/Jet Blaziken/Gyarados—matching the registered Intim/Fairy physical core over Scarf/FG this game.
decisions.notebook: Matchup: opp physical core Mega Blaziken Speed Boost, Kingambit, Gyarados, Excadrill + Prankster Whimsicott + Gengar Sash. Answer with Mega Floette Fairy Aura, Intim H-Arcanine, Adapt Bascu Wave Crash/Jet, Annihilape CC (4x Gambit)+Rage Fist. Pult Scarf speed/Ghost; Maushold FG/FM support. Prefer Intim+Aura offense. Game1 mode: Floette+Arcanine lead, Ape+Bascu back. Watch Tailwind then priority/Jet; Sash Gengar Poison on Floette.

decisions.rationale: Prankster Tailwind is unstoppable and enables Blaziken/Gyarados endgame and beats Scarf Dragapult. Gengar already outspeeds both foes; Sludge Bomb is 2x into Floette (59-100%, possible OHKO) and removes the Light of Ruin threat. If Floette Protects, we lose nothing—Tailwind is up and we re-attack next turn. Sash Gengar survives any single hit; Sitrus Whimsicott may tank Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Blaziken is the planned Mega and best immediate answer: in Tailwind it hits 334 Spe, outspeeds even Scarf Dragapult, CC OHKOes Arcanine-H through 74%, and Knock Off covers Dragapult/Basculegion. Gyarados risks Defiant Annihilape and 4x Thunderbolt from Dragapult. Gengar passes; it still outspeeds all foes in Tailwind for a parting Shadow Ball.

decisions.rationale: Both my mons move first (356/290 vs 98-142). Shadow Ball (58-106%) + Mega Knock Off (40-75%, plus unmodeled item-removal boost) guarantees the Basculegion KO bar Protect, removing the only OHKO threat to Blaziken. Arcanine can't KO Blaziken in one hit (ESpeed ~40%, Flare Blitz resisted, Rock Slide chip) and Gengar's intact Focus Sash guarantees it fires. Mega now banks a Speed Boost so Blaziken (334 in Tailwind) outspeeds max Scarf Dragapult (319) for the endgame; next turn CC deletes Arcanine.

Plan this series: Tailwind mode with Mega Blaziken as wincon; Gyarados (Power Whip SE vs Basculegion) as mid-game pivot; Kingambit/Excadrill benched vs this matchup.

reflections.summary: Won because the preview plan was validated: opponent benched Dragapult (their only real speed control), so Mega Blaziken's Speed Boost snowballed unopposed to +6 while Gyarados covered the whole enemy bring (4x Waterfall KO on Arcanine-H, Power Whip/Waterfall pressure on Basculegion and Annihilape). The opponent's Annihilape Protect-stall with Leftovers actively fed us free Speed Boost turns; chip from Flare Blitz + Waterfall outpaced the healing and the third consecutive Protect failed on turn
reflections.adjustment: Expect game-2 counter-picking: Dragapult (Scarf speed control) and possibly Maushold (Follow Me to shield Annihilape from double-target pressure) are the obvious ins. Keep the same core but plan for Pult — bank +2/+3 Speed on Blaziken via Protect-stalling before Pult enters (or +1 under Tailwind), hold Gyarados Ice Fang and Gengar Shadow Ball as Dragapult answers, and re-scout preview rather than auto-locking the identical four.

Tendencies: opponent will attempt THREE+ consecutive Protects under sustained double-target pressure (third failed turn 8) - their stall hands us free Speed Boost turns, so mirror with our own Protects and let boosts compound; Annihilape so far played purely as CC-into-Blaziken + Protect/Leftovers stall, never Rage Fist or Drain Punch, so Rage Fist stacking not yet a demonstrated threat; Floette-Mega played as Fairy Aura nuke. Game-2 prep: expect Dragapult in for speed control and/or Maushold Follow Me to protect Annihilape; keep Ice Fang Gyarados + Shadow Ball Gengar as Pult answer

reflections.summary: Lost due to flawed team-preview: Mega Floette + Intim Arcanine lead (Ape/Bascu back) mismatched vs Whimsicott Tailwind + Mega Blaziken Speed Boost + Gyarados, letting Speed snowball and Arcanine die early to Waterfall while Ape Protect-stalled futilely.
reflections.adjustment: Change preview mode—lead Ape+Bascu (or Bascu+Floette) to pressure Blaziken before Boosts stack; keep Floette Mega only if Tailwind can be denied, else prioritize immediate offense over Intim+Aura.
